Which actions a shade accepts depends on how it was learned by Bond; an action the shade does not support returns a Bond error that the driver surfaces in Status. ToggleOpen and Hold are offered only when the shade's action list reports them.

One metric per driver instance. Add another instance for a second series — the ledger is deliberately single-series so its storage ceiling stays predictable.

Sampling is interval polling, not change subscription, so a spike between two samples is not seen.

Bucket keys come from the controller local calendar. On the fall-back DST day the repeated local hour merges into one hourly bucket, so that bucket covers two real hours; its count and sum stay correct but the bucket is wider.
Daily buckets are folded from sealed hourly buckets, so the open hour is not yet reflected in the current day total.

Under Aggregates Only and Paused there are no raw rows, so Window Summary and the min/max/average/trend variables describe the most recent hourly bucket rather than a rolling window of the last N samples.
This driver renders no charts. It produces the numbers and the export; the picture belongs to whatever you feed it to.
Export is capped at 500 rows, so a longer history must be pulled in successive exports as it ages through the rings.

Matrix/Tile for LIFX Tile, Candle, Ceiling, Path, Spot, Tube, Luna and Mirror: paint the whole matrix one color via Set64 (one 522-byte message per tile, and per 64-zone band on wide devices), and run the MORPH, FLAME, or SKY firmware effect via SetTileEffect — capability comes from the product id or a StateDeviceChain reply, which also hands over the real chain geometry

Relay power for the LIFX Switch: Relay On / Off / Toggle over SetRPower with the relay's own position read back over GetRPower, plus a Relay Changed event when someone presses the physical button — a relay switches a DUMB load, so the driver reports the relay's position and never pretends to know the load is lit, and there is no dimming because the protocol defines none

A confirmed LIFX Switch is treated as what LIFX calls it — a 'non light'. Power, Set Color and Set White are refused by name on it, its poll reads the relay instead of asking for light state it is documented to discard, and its StateUnhandled replies count as proof of life so a perfectly reachable switch never sits at DEVICE_ONLINE false

Light effects for any confirmed light — Flash, Pulse and Breathe over SetWaveform (103), packed byte-exactly at its documented 21 bytes with transient set so the light always lands back on the color it started from. Flash and Breathe use the SINE waveform, the only one LIFX documents as returning within every cycle; Pulse adds the documented skew_ratio duty cycle. Effect Channels can route the effect through SetWaveformOptional (119) instead, so you can flash the porch light on brightness alone without turning it a different color
Polled State (Light Get/State) publishes POWER, HUE, SAT, BRIGHTNESS, KELVIN, and DEVICE_ONLINE; an EchoRequest keepalive proves reachability

Replies correlated by source + sequence and de-duplicated against late/duplicate datagrams; no token or key of any kind leaves the controller; MAC-locked IntegrateIT licensing on every control path

LAN broadcast reachability is required: discovery and control are sent to the subnet broadcast address and targeted by the bulb's serial. If the controller and bulb are on different subnets/VLANs, or broadcast is filtered, the bulb will not be found or controlled.

MultiZone covers LIFX Z / Beam strips via SetExtendedColorZones (510): per-zone color, gradients, and the Move effect. Extended zones need recent strip firmware (older LIFX Z may need a firmware update); the legacy SetColorZones (501) path is not written, and zone commands are refused until capability is positively confirmed.

Matrix covers whole-matrix color (Set64, 715) and the MORPH / FLAME / SKY firmware effects (SetTileEffect, 719). Per-zone matrix patterns, animations, and reading the matrix back (Get64/State64, 707/711) are not written — Set Matrix Color paints one color across every zone. The driver also does not read a running effect back (StateTileEffect, 720), so no variable claims which effect is active. SKY is documented by LIFX as LIFX Ceiling on firmware 4.4 or newer only; this driver cannot check firmware version, so on other matrix devices the SKY selection is simply ignored by the device.

The end-of-cycle indication is a boolean in the protocol — no brightness or power level for it exists to expose.

Relays cover the LIFX Switch's electrical outputs (GetRPower 816 / SetRPower 817 / StateRPower 818) and nothing else. A relay switches a DUMB load: the driver can report the relay's POSITION, which is all the switch tells it, and can never know whether the lamp on the other side is actually lit — a dead bulb, a pulled fixture and a lamp switched off at its own body all read identically. There is no dimming: LIFX documents that current switch models cannot dim and that 0 and 65535 are the only valid levels, so those are the only two this driver sends and no relay-level property is offered.

The number of relays on a LIFX Switch is not published anywhere official — not in the LAN protocol, not on LIFX's own LIFX Switch page, and not in the products registry, which carries no relay-count field. So the Relay Index property exposes the full 0-255 range the protocol's own u8 relay_index allows rather than inventing a count, and the relay variables only ever report what a real StateRPower reply said. Point Relay Index at a relay that does not exist and the switch simply will not answer.

The switch's physical BUTTONS are not read. LIFX documents button messages, but this driver implements only the three relay messages, so a button press shows up only as the Relay Changed that follows it when that button is wired to a relay — a button configured to drive a cloud scene produces nothing here at all.

Light effects (SetWaveform 103 / SetWaveformOptional 119) are fire-and-forget, and deliberately so. LIFX documents both packets as returning a LightState (107) — that is the ordinary response-to-a-Set reporting the light's state at that instant, not a completion report — and the protocol defines no GetWaveform, no StateWaveform, and no message that cancels a running effect. So no variable or event claims an effect is running, finished, or was accepted, and the way to keep an effect short is to keep Effect Cycles x period short. Effect Cycles is whole numbers only (1-255): the protocol carries that field as an IEEE-754 float32 and this driver packs bytes arithmetically in Lua 5.1, so it offers the integer domain it can encode byte-exactly rather than approximating a fraction. SAW and TRIANGLE are documented waveforms that no command here sends. Effects treat a strip or matrix as ONE zone — LIFX documents that plainly — so a whole Z / Beam / Ceiling flashes as a single color.
State feedback is by polling, not push: a change made from the LIFX app appears on the next poll (default 10s), not instantly. Unsolicited/streamed state is not subscribed to.
Discovery lists a bulb by its serial (12-hex). Friendly labels (SetLabel/StateLabel) and firmware/version reads are not surfaced in this version.
The LIFX LAN protocol is unauthenticated by design (no token, password, or key on the wire). Use it only on a trusted LAN segment; anyone on the same broadcast domain can address the bulb.

The driver does not enumerate, probe, or interrogate remotes. It classifies only the activity Composer bindings or programming hand it, so a remote that is never linked and never programmed is never detected.
Battery level is reported in, not read out: the driver publishes and thresholds whatever LEVEL a programming step supplies. It does not poll a remote battery variable.

Button text depends entirely on what the source supplies. Most BUTTON_LINK presses carry no button name, so Full Detail commonly reads "(button not reported)" for binding detections; button text is reliable only from the Report Remote Activity command's BUTTON parameter.
Headless: it publishes who is driving the room, it does not itself control any load.

TLS reality: UniFi consoles present a self-signed certificate. By default the driver sets the C4:url ssl_verify_peer/ssl_verify_host options to off, which is what makes a self-signed console reachable — the simulator does not model TLS, so this specific behavior is verified on hardware, not in the sim. Fingerprint pinning is not offered because the Control4 URL API has no documented pin option; the alternative is TLS Verification = Full with a console certificate the controller OS trusts.

On OS builds without C4:url() the driver falls back to the legacy urlGet/urlPost path, which has no per-request TLS options — a self-signed console will likely be unreachable there. Practical floor for self-signed consoles is an OS with C4:url().

Presence and device-health scanning read up to 200 entries per poll (one page). On a site whose client or device list exceeds one page, the driver holds state rather than inventing it: a watched client absent from the page it fetched is kept at its last-known presence (never false-declared offline), and device-health change events are suppressed until a full page is seen again. The trade-off on such large sites is that a watched client which genuinely leaves may not raise Went Offline until it once again fits within a single page.

Presence is polled, not pushed: a watched phone joining or leaving is seen on the next poll (default 30s), then offline is debounced by the Offline After (polls) setting to ride out brief Wi-Fi drops.

The PoE power-cycle action requires the target port to actually deliver PoE; the console accepts the action per its own firmware rules and the driver surfaces the HTTP result. It is the only write this driver performs, and it is disabled until Enable PoE Power Cycle is set to Yes.
API keys exist only on UniFi OS consoles — the legacy self-hosted Java controller is not supported, by Ubiquiti's design.
